title: Kryptos K4
origin: Fourth passage of Jim Sanborn's sculpture Kryptos at CIA headquarters, Langley, Virginia (1990)

hints.hint: "Two events had a significant role to play while I was writing the plain text of Kryptos in 1988. The first was my second trip to Egypt in late 1986, and the second was the fall of the Berlin Wall."
hints.given: Open letter of November 2025, as quoted by Popular Mechanics on 19 November 2025

hints.hint: "The Berlin Clock in K4 is the World Clock in Berlin that was the gathering place for the crowds that brought down the Berlin wall."
hints.given: Open letter of November 2025, as quoted by Popular Mechanics on 19 November 2025

hints.hint: "The codes of Kryptos from the morse code at the beginning through K5 are about delivering a message." K5 is a further passage that the artist has announced and not yet released.
hints.given: Open letter of November 2025, as quoted by Popular Mechanics on 19 November 2025

hints.hint: Writing about a future owner who might not keep K4 secret: "If they don't, then (CLUE) what's the point?"

verification.how: The owner of the artist's solution runs an online verifier that compares a submitted plaintext with a stored hash of the artist's text.

notes: Positions are counted from 1. The fragments were published by the artist as hints.
The plaintext was located among the artist's archived papers in 2025 and has not been published; the cipher method is still unknown.
